patch.value: Trajectory projection: read the immutable record as an ordered observation-action-outcome sequence per episode or session, streamed and resumable, so training, offline evaluation and fleet analytics share one derived artifact

Running episodes produces the artifact that training, offline evaluation and fleet analysis all actually consume: a sequence of what the agent saw, what it did, and what followed. pm records the middle term of that sequence completely and permanently -- 40,446 history entries across 2,165 streams in this workspace alone, every mutation with author, harness, operation, patch and hash chain -- and offers no way to read it as a trajectory.

The gap is not storage, it is shape. History is stored per item, which is the correct primary key for reconstructing an item and the wrong one for reconstructing a run. An agent session touches many items; an episode spans many streams; a trajectory is ordered by causality across all of them. Assembling one today means reading every stream, filtering by identity, and re-ordering by wall-clock timestamp -- which pm-10l1vm already establishes is not a sound causal order across concurrently recorded streams, and which pm-z2j1qt shows costs 1.59M tokens to even attempt through the one command that reads the record.

What is missing is a derived, episode-scoped or session-scoped projection over the immutable record: an ordered sequence of steps, each carrying the observation boundary that was in force, the mutation that was recorded, the identity that recorded it including harness, model and effort once pm-ffz0a9 makes the model resolvable, and the verdict deltas that followed. Emitted as line-delimited rows so it streams in constant memory at any length, per the uniform row-streaming contract pm-mav1ak defines, and resumable by cursor so a decade of runs is readable in bounded working memory.

Four consumers, one artifact.

Training needs the sequence as supervision: which action followed which observation, and what the recorded outcome was. The reward term comes from computed criterion verdicts rather than from a hand-written scorer, which is the property pm-nfrhf0 exists to establish.

Offline evaluation needs to replay a recorded trajectory against a different policy without re-running the environment, which requires that the observation boundary be part of the record rather than reconstructed by guesswork.

Fleet analytics needs it as the join key for per-harness and per-model throughput, rework and defect-escape rates, which pm-gw6uyq wants to derive from immutable history alone and currently has no trajectory to derive them from.

Post-hoc audit needs it to answer why an agent did what it did, which is the same question pm-f86lth asks of source files and this asks of behaviour.

Two constraints follow from the record being immutable and the project being long-lived. The projection is derived and never authoritative: it must be recomputable from history alone, so a rebuilt index and a fresh read agree, and no trajectory row is ever a source of truth. And it must respect the redaction and retention machinery -- a redacted history entry must not resurface inside a trajectory export, which makes this a consumer of the retention policy owned by pm-h6wmtc rather than an exception to it.

This item owns the trajectory projection and its streaming, resumable read contract. It does not own the episode runtime that generates trajectories, the causal ordering identity that makes cross-stream order sound, or the retention policy it must honour -- each is a declared dependency with an existing owner.

A trajectory is readable scoped to an episode or a session, ordered by a sound causal order rather than wall-clock timestamp alone; Each step carries the observation boundary in force, the recorded mutation, the recording identity including harness, model and effort where available, and any verdict change that followed; Output is line-delimited rows read in constant memory at any trajectory length, and a cursor resumes an interrupted read; The projection is derived and recomputable from history alone: a rebuilt index and a fresh read produce identical trajectories, and no trajectory row is ever authoritative; Redacted history content never resurfaces in a trajectory export, proven by a test that redacts an entry and re-reads a trajectory covering it; The read is bounded by a declared token budget like every other read surface, and degrades rather than emitting unbounded output

message: Filed as the output-side counterpart to pm-li2fj5. Duplicate check: searched training/dataset/export/replay/trajectory and episode/step/observation; the closest matches are pm-4a7m and pm-pjs5 (closed history-maintenance primitives) and pm-tqel (command placement), none of which produces a cross-stream run-ordered projection. Depends on pm-10l1vm because pm-10l1vm establishes that wall-clock order across concurrent streams is not causal order.
